claims.text: Eric Carlson is reported as confirming that three or four Echo Flight missiles went off alert, against Robert Salas's claim of all ten. On this specific point the released 341st SMW unit history supports Salas and not Carlson: it states that all launch facilities in E Flight lost strategic alert nearly simultaneously.

THE CONTENTS OF THE 1 OCTOBER 1996 LETTER ARE DISPUTED AND THE BOARD HAS NOT READ IT. Salas and Hastings present it as elaborating and supporting the Oscar Flight account. Sceptical sources quote it as recording that Meiwald's recollection differs from Salas's and that he regrets being unable to help Salas establish his claims. Both characterisations are recorded; neither is adopted.

claims.sourceText: Metabunk skeptical resources thread on Salas and Malmstrom, https://www.metabunk.org/threads/ufos-at-nuclear-weapons-sites-salas-malmstrom-eagle-flight-skeptical-resources.3284/ , opened 2026-09-19
claims.text: James Carlson states that Figel told him he saw no UFO and treated the radio report as a joke, and that both Figel and Eric Carlson reported no UFOs at Echo Flight.

His enumerated disputes with Robert Salas are: that Salas claims all ten Echo Flight missiles shut down where Eric Carlson confirms three or four; that no Oscar Flight incident occurred on 24 or 25 March 1967; that Walt Figel denied seeing a UFO; that Salas has located himself inconsistently across accounts; and that Salas never witnessed anything directly, his account being of a telephone call from a topside security policeman.

James Carlson, son of Echo Flight crew commander Capt. Eric D. Carlson, has published a 357-page work titled 'American, Credulous' and a shorter piece titled 'Echo Flights of Fantasy - Anatomy of a UFO Hoax', concluding that no UFOs were involved at Echo Flight or any other flight and that claims of UFO interference are completely unsupportable.

claims.sourceText: Reported via the Hastings material, https://www.metabunk.org/threads/ufos-at-nuclear-weapons-sites-salas-malmstrom-eagle-flight-skeptical-resources.3284/ , opened 2026-09-19
claims.text: A remark attributed to Boeing engineer Robert Kaminski about the Echo Flight missiles, that they were perfect and clean, is reported as having been made to Arneson. This is a relayed recollection of a remark and is carried at Tier 3 on that basis.

An external attribution circulates that this board has NOT opened: a Top Secret 1969 USAF official history, Bernard C. Nalty's 'USAF Ballistic Missile Programs 1967-1968', is quoted second-hand as recording that an electronic noise pulse had shut down the flight, similar to the electromagnetic pulse generated by nuclear explosions. Nalty was not opened and the claim is carried at Tier 2 on that basis.

claims.text: Col. Frederick Meiwald wrote to Robert Salas about the March 1967 events on 1 October 1996, after Salas located him in the summer of that year. The letter is published by Salas and Robert Hastings. IT HAS NOT BEEN OPENED BY THIS BOARD and two flatly incompatible characterisations of its contents are in public circulation: that it elaborates and supports the Oscar Flight account, and that it records Meiwald's recollection as differing from Salas's and regrets being unable to help him establish his claims.

Col. Frederick Meiwald wrote to Salas about the incident on 1 October 1996. THE LETTER HAS NOT BEEN OPENED BY THIS BOARD and two incompatible characterisations of it are in circulation, one supporting and one contradicting Salas. Kevin Randle separately records Salas giving all ten missiles and Meiwald four or five.

James Carlson disputes that any Oscar Flight incident occurred, citing SAC UFO officer Col. Lewis D. Chase as finding no equipment failures or sighting on that date, and disputes Salas's account of the flight to which he was assigned.

claims.text: In a 1997 letter to researcher Jim Klotz, Boeing engineer Robert Kaminski wrote that the Echo Flight investigation team found no significant failures, engineering data or findings that would explain how ten missiles were knocked off alert, and that the Air Force unexpectedly ordered the inquiry ended mid-stream with no report to be filed.
